clue.text: Duck could be left out for stuffing

indicators.note: out says the letter is to be left out of the longer word

parts.note: a duck could be waddling, walking with a side-to-side gait

explanation.surface: A duck might be dropped from a recipe for stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the noun to define; it is the bird doing what ducks do.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadding is soft padding material used for stuffing or lining.

clue.text: Send forth an English team abroad

indicators.note: abroad, meaning astray or all over the place, signals a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English side is sent off to play overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, i.e. to send forth.

clue.text: Working studiously without first taking a rest

indicators.note: without first drops the opening letter of the word

parts.note: plying means working steadily and diligently at something, as in plying a trade

explanation.surface: A student stops working hard and takes a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying down is taking a rest, so lying is a synonym in the participle form.

clue.text: Consider one in colony looking back heraldically

parts.note: to regard is to consider
an ant is one member of an ant colony

explanation.surface: Think of a single member of a colony as it glances behind, in heraldic terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, regardant describes a beast with its head turned to look backwards.

clue.text: Rod entangled in framework for rigging ropes

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the framework word

parts.note: a cage is a framework of bars

indicators.note: entangled means the letters of rod are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishing rod gets caught up in a frame meant for a ship's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordage is the collective term for ropes, especially those in a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Indian's line — making a basket

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American's line is used to weave a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket, especially one anglers use to carry fish.

clue.text: A fall after drinks in which one comes back eventually

definitions.text: in which one comes back eventually

indicators.note: after puts the fall at the end, following the drinks

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: A tumble after a round of drinks, with someone stumbling home.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey out and back again, so the traveller returns at the end.

clue.text: Sailor's forlorn seafood

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
forlorn means lonely, alone

explanation.surface: A lonely sailor eats a seafood meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, a prized type of seafood.

clue.text: Gray, say, was celeb at heart with significance

indicators.note: at heart takes the inner letters of celeb, dropping its first and last

parts.note: the gist is the main point or significance

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Gray was a celebrity of real importance.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'; 'say' marks him as one example. 'was' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist is a writer of elegies, and the poet Thomas Gray is a famous example.

clue.text: See 1
Teach a bit in mid-week

indicators.note: in puts the coin inside the middle letters of the week
mid- picks out the central letters of the following word

parts.note: a bit can be a coin (a threepenny bit), and a ducat is an old coin

explanation.surface: An instruction to do some teaching in the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-week' looks like Wednesday, but 'mid-' works on the word 'week' itself; 'a bit' is a coin, as in a threepenny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone is to teach them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Launching in river outside summer month

indicators.note: outside here puts the river on the outer end, after the month

parts.note: taken as written
Aug is the abbreviation for August, a summer month
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Something is set up in a river beyond the summer months.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the launching or opening one, used adjectivally as in an inaugural voyage.

clue.text: Small house in revised bid for washer

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the reworked word
revised means the letters of bid are set out afresh

parts.note: small signals an abbreviation, and HO is short for house

explanation.surface: A small house appears in a fresh offer for a washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhobi is an Indian washerman, so a washer of clothes by trade.

clue.text: Diving bird seen returning among the icebergs

indicators.note: seen returning means the letters found are read back to front
among says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird that dives is spotted coming back through the icebergs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' finds EBERG inside 'icebergs'; 'seen returning' turns it round. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a waterbird famous for diving underwater after fish.

clue.text: A leader, I do article not about to be changed

indicators.note: to be changed means the remaining letters are rearranged
not tells us to drop the letter for about

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone vows to leave an article alone, unchanged, as the paper's lead piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not about' removes C from IDOARTICLE, leaving IDOARTILE for 'to be changed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader, or leading article, is the newspaper's editorial giving its opinion.

clue.text: Ground hot and barren? Horrible!

indicators.note: ground, as in crushed or milled, signals the letters being broken up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at land that is scorched and infertile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as land described by the next words, but it is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the two fodder words and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent is detestable or loathsome, a synonym of horrible.

clue.text: Sweet store — for a maze of cavities?

definitions.meaning: a place where sweet stuff is stored, wax cells holding the bees' supply
anything riddled with holes, a mass of hollows like a sponge

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeycomb stores honey, and figuratively describes anything full of cells or holes.

clue.text: Put in order mostly strict as an officer of the church

indicators.note: put in order means the letters of the first words are rearranged
mostly drops the final letter of strict

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instruction to tidy up strictly, as befits a church official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter from 'strict'; 'Put in order' rearranges what is left with AS, and 'an' stays as it is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan is the church official in charge of the sacristy and its vessels and vestments.

clue.text: Temporary residence of child taking in a day abroad

indicators.note: taking in puts the French day inside the child

parts.note: a son is a child
jour is French for day

explanation.surface: A child's short stay abroad lasting a day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere.

clue.text: Oxbridge feature with building item (mainly the fabric)

parts.note: the Cam is the river running through Cambridge, one half of Oxbridge

indicators.note: mainly drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: a brick is an item used in building

explanation.surface: A Cambridge feature built of bricks makes up most of the fabric of the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fabric' looks like the building's structure; it is cloth. Oxbridge means Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, dense white linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: A small growth in college parking

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of British college
P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Something growing slowly in a college car park.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal growth of tissue, for instance in the nose or bowel.

clue.text: He precedes me in the elemental order

definitions.text: He precedes me in the elemental order

parts.words: He precedes me in the elemental order
parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, number 2 in the periodic table; the speaker is the next element

explanation.walkthrough: 'He' reads as a pronoun but is the symbol for helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithium is element number 3, coming directly after helium in the periodic table.

clue.text: A model bit of writing's lost, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: para, a paragraph, is a bit of writing, and lost means gone

explanation.surface: Part of a manuscript has gone missing, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: PARA + GONE said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example.

clue.text: 50% gobbledegook from one in the clouds?

indicators.note: 50% keeps only one half of the phrase, dropping the other

parts.note: gobbledegook is meaningless talk, and the usual two-word rhyming phrase for it has two halves; only the second is kept

explanation.surface: Half of someone's talk is nonsense from a dreamer with their head in the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in the clouds?' sounds like a daydreamer; it is a jumbo jet, flying among the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbo is a jumbo jet, a large airliner that flies up among the clouds.

clue.text: Money official distressed at ramp? Yes

indicators.note: distressed indicates the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: The fuel including last trace of coal in a fold

indicators.note: including puts the letter inside the fuel word

parts.note: peat is a fuel dug from bogs

indicators.note: last trace of picks the final letter of coal

explanation.surface: Fuel with the remains of coal tucked into a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into cloth.

clue.text: Vehicle's colour, disregarding extremities

indicators.note: disregarding extremities drops the first and last letters

parts.note: magenta is a purplish-red colour

explanation.surface: Someone describes the paintwork of a car, ignoring the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' looks like a car, but it is the definition in its sense of a means or medium; ''s' is a link.

clue.text: This country's weather feature, we hear? No, another country

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said and judged by their sound

parts.note: this country, in a British paper, is the UK, and its famous weather feature is rain

explanation.walkthrough: 'UK rain' spoken sounds like the answer. 'No' dismisses this country to point to the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe, different from the UK named first.

clue.text: Number 1 or 2 of 11

parts.note: in a cricket eleven, the players listed first and second in the batting order go in together to start the innings

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket teams have eleven players; the two who bat first open the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the first two in the eleven's batting order start the innings, so they are its openers.
